title: Palworld Endgame Guide | Feybreak, Sunreach and the World Tree Explained | Palworld Guide
description: The full Palworld 1.0 endgame path: Feybreak and the Bjorn & Bastigor tower, the portal to Sunreach, the six barrier devices and Auri & Shaolong, the Panthalus quest and the World Tree, plus raids, the best combat Pals and how to prepare.

sections.heading: The road to the endgame
sections.script: Palworld one point zero added a whole new endgame, and it can be confusing to know where to go. In this guide I will walk you through the full path, step by step. First Feybreak and its tower, then the portal to the Sunreach sky islands, then the final regular tower, and finally the World Tree, the endgame region with the strongest Pals in the game. Along the way we will cover raid bosses, the best Pals to bring, and how to prepare so you don't get wiped out. Everything here is based on up to date one point zero guides. Let's go.

sections.heading: Before you leave Palpagos
sections.script: The adventure starts on the Palpagos Islands, the main map. Here you fight your first tower bosses, like Zoe and Grizzbolt, Lily and Lyleen, Axel and Orserk, Marcus and Faleris, and Victor and Shadowbeak. Each one tests a different element, so it pays to build a team that covers several types. Remember that tower fights in one point zero have a five minute timer, so they are really damage checks. Use these fights to level up, because the level cap is now eighty, and the later regions expect you to be much stronger than you are at the start.

sections.heading: Feybreak and Bjorn
sections.script: Your next big stop is Feybreak. The key location is the Feybreak Tower at the southern edge of Feybreak Island. Inside waits Bjorn with Bastigor. Bastigor is an Ice Pal, so Fire Pals are your best friends here. Bastigor is also the best Cooling Pal in the game, so it is worth catching later for your base. Beating Bjorn and Bastigor is the gate to everything that follows, because it opens the portal at the top of the tower. Take your time in Feybreak, level up, and gather strong Pals before you take the portal.

sections.heading: Into Sunreach
sections.script: After you beat Bjorn and Bastigor, step through the portal on top of the Feybreak Tower. It drops you into Sunreach, a group of sky islands high above the world. Sunreach is a high level area. Guides strongly recommend being around level seventy before you explore it. The only way to move between the islands is to fly, so bring a good flying mount. Unlock the Watchtowers as you go, so you can fast travel and avoid long trips. Sunreach is also home to Jetragon, which now waits here as a level seventy Alpha at Dragonmark Peak.

sections.heading: The six barrier devices and Auri
sections.script: The big goal in Sunreach is the final regular tower, the fight against Auri and Shaolong. But the tower is protected. First, you have to find and shut down all six barrier devices around Auri's tower. Once all six are off, you can enter. Shaolong is Water and Dragon, so Electric and Ice Pals work best. Shaolong is also the best Watering Pal in the game, so it is a fantastic catch for your base later. Beating Auri and Shaolong means you have cleared every regular tower, which is the key to the World Tree.

sections.heading: The Panthalus quest
sections.script: Now the World Tree quest opens up. Talk to the Ancient Civilization Researcher on the Deserted Islet. You will need to collect Echobones from ancient whale remains, and use them to craft the Echoing Flute. With the flute, you summon the legendary whale Pal, Panthalus. Here is the most important tip in this whole video: you need to capture Panthalus, not just defeat it. Bring your strongest spheres. Once Panthalus is in your party, go to the World Tree terminal at the sealed barrier and interact with it to open the way.

sections.heading: The World Tree
sections.script: The World Tree is the endgame region of Palworld one point zero, a level seventy to eighty area with the strongest Pals in the game. This is where many of the best base workers come from, like Solenne for Handiwork, Renjishi for Kindling, Dandilord for Planting and Silvance for Medicine. It is also where you will find some of the toughest fights. Explore carefully, upgrade your gear, and bring a balanced team. If you have read this far, you already know the route. Now it is all about getting stronger.

sections.heading: Raid bosses
sections.script: Raids are another big part of the endgame. To start one, build the Summoning Altar from the Ancient Technology tree. It can only be built inside a base. Then collect four slab fragments for the boss you want, from chests, expeditions and earlier raids, and craft them into that boss's slab. Place the slab on the altar and the raid begins, with a timer of about ten minutes. Raid bosses like Bellanoir and Blazamut Ryu are tough, but they are also where some of the strongest Pals in the game come from.

sections.heading: The best Pals to bring
sections.script: Which Pals should you take into the endgame? Guides rank Frostallion, Blazamut Ryu and Jormuntide Ignis at the very top for combat. The raid Pals, Bellanoir Libero and Selyne, deal the most damage against raid bosses. Jetragon is still the safest all round pick. And if you don't want to hunt legendaries, Jormuntide Ignis is the strongest non legendary attacker, and it is much easier to breed than the raid Pals. Always bring a mix of elements, so you can answer whatever boss you face.

sections.heading: Catching the legendaries
sections.script: The endgame is also when most players go after the legendary Pals, and one point zero made them tougher. Frostallion, Paladius and Necromus were level fifty in early access, and now all three are level sixty. Frostallion waits at a frozen lake in the Astral Mountains, so bring Fire Pals and warm gear. Paladius and Necromus share one arena in the desert, and you can only summon one of them at a time, so plan two trips. Jetragon jumped to level seventy and moved to the Sunreach sky islands. Bring your best spheres, weaken them carefully, and don't give up after a miss.

sections.heading: Endgame mounts
sections.script: Getting around the endgame regions takes a good flying mount, especially in Sunreach where flying is the only way between islands. Most rankings put Jetragon and Xenolord at the very top. Jetragon is the classic speed king, and Xenolord is great for long flights. Frostallion is also a strong all round mount if you already caught it. Remember that every mount needs its saddle before you can ride it, so unlock the saddle as soon as you catch a new mount. A fast flyer saves you hours of travel in the late game.

sections.heading: How to prepare
sections.script: Before each new region, prepare properly. Level up toward the cap of eighty. Condense your best fighters and workers, since reaching four stars raises every work suitability by one, and maxing out now needs only forty eight Pals in total. Collect Lifmunk Effigies and offer them at a Statue of Power to raise your capture rate, which makes catching legendaries much easier. Keep a strong base running with Anubis, Knocklem and your World Tree workers, so you always have the gear, spheres and food you need.

sections.heading: See you in the World Tree
sections.script: So that is the full endgame path: Palpagos towers, Feybreak and Bjorn, the portal to Sunreach, the six barrier devices and Auri, the Panthalus quest, and finally the World Tree, with raids along the way. Where are you on this path right now, and which part gave you the most trouble? Tell me in the comments, and let me know which boss you want a full guide for next.
